summary: Read-only investigation: what it takes to train the GEO2b energy models (AW/GNN/TF/XGB) on D0+D1, with costs and leakage risks

facts: All 10 targets exist for D0. Repo-root labels_all.json (sha256 62c0e784…, identical in the main checkout and the geo1 worktree) has 5,265 records, and every record has numeric d1_kcal, d2_kcal, elst_dft, pauli_dft, oi_dft, disp_dft, cpcm_dft, cds_dft, bsse_shift_kcal and barrier_kcal, plus eint_spe_kcal, e_bond_kcal, e_*_eh and eda_raw_eh. There are no NaN or null values. The field names are the same keys D1 uses (d1pair_common.D1_TCOL: c_ghost = bsse_shift_kcal, barrier = barrier_kcal). So D1_TCOL can read D0 records unchanged.

/gpfs/tmp_cpu2/yeseo1ee/espley_rev6/S/S_targets.parquet (sha256 6b02630f…) was built by analysis/espley_xtb_repro/r6_split.py from the status-ok rows of labels_all.json (5,260 rows). It has 14 columns: rxn_id, dft_d1_kcal, dft_d2_kcal, dft_eint_spe_kcal, dft_barrier_kcal, dft_e_bond_kcal, dft_elst_dft, dft_pauli_dft, dft_oi_dft, dft_disp_dft, dft_cpcm_dft, dft_cds_dft, bsse_shift_kcal and dft_c_ghost_kcal. dft_c_ghost_kcal is derived as barrier − d1 − d2 − e_bond. On the rev 6 C rows it equals bsse_shift_kcal to at most 5.0e-10 (results_rev6/S_label_checks.json; max |eint − e_bond − bsse_shift| = 0.0). d1pair_common.D0_TCOL maps the targets to these dft_* names.

Target definitions are the same in D0 and D1 (method ①, label_true/scripts/stage3_parse.parse_one_rxn; the D1 copy has the same sha256 413bd2a7…; EH_TO_KCAL = 627.5094740631; all values in kcal/mol). d1/d2 = E(frag*_dist) − E(frag*_rel). eint_spe = E(AB) − E(frag1_dist) − E(frag2_dist). barrier = E(TS) − E(frag1_rel) − E(frag2_rel), an electronic SP barrier, not Coley's G_act. It equals d1 + d2 + eint_spe within 1e-6 (gate G1). c_ghost = bsse_shift_kcal = eint_spe − e_bond = sum of the ghost-basis shifts of the two fragments. The 6 EDA channels come from ORCA's EDA table. Checked by hand on rxn 0: 10.0418 + 3.9759 − 10.3371 = 3.6806 = barrier_kcal, and bsse_shift 0.16286 = shift1 0.01200 + shift2 0.15086.

Geometries differ by engine. The D1 energy labels the LADDER/GEO2 models train on are not labels_d1_g2.json. labels_d1_g2.json (9,266 rows, all ok) is a verbatim copy of labels_d1.json rows (analysis/d1_g2/prep_g.py) and uses the original Coley-rule references. The model y is /gpfs/tmp_cpu2/yeseo1ee/d1_ladder/F_pairs_cr2.csv (8,389 pairs; D1LADDER.md 4-1; GEO2 gate L-11), built from labels_d1_cr2.json. cr2 re-assigns references: Q = the lowest label-level reference energy per molecule key (RDKit canonical isomeric SMILES, enantiomers merged, constrained dipoles kept separate), replaced when > 0.05 kcal/mol. V = an extra xTB+DFT conformer search. Only d1, d2 and barrier change. Q changed 3,100 reactions; 3,131 of 9,266 changed vs the original (V_summary.md). The originals are kept under the 'orig' key of each cr2 record. elst, pauli, oi, disp, cpcm, cds and c_ghost equal F_pairs.csv to 1e-12.

D0 has no cr or cr2 correction. Its references are Coley's per-reaction reactant files (rel1_file/rel2_file from full_dataset_profiles/<rxn>/r*.xyz). alt_used = 1 in 3,037 rows (_alt dipole reference) and 0 in 2,228. D1's original reference rule is a port of Coley's rule (A4: 24/24 agree), so D0 matches D1-orig, not D1-cr2. A quick check (formula only, so not exact molecule keys) shows the same within-molecule spread in D0 dipolarophile references. Spread of e_frag2_rel_eh: C2H4, 108 reactions, 0.013 kcal/mol; C7H10N2O, 442 reactions, 0.46; C5H8O, 194, 2.98; C9H14, 682, 9.99.

problems: d1, d2 and barrier cannot be used as-is together with the D1 y. The D1 y uses cr2 (lowest reference per molecule key + V conformers). D0 uses Coley's per-reaction reference, the same rule as D1-orig, which differs from cr2 in 3,131 of 9,266 D1 reactions. Mixing them puts reference-conformer noise into D0 d1/d2/barrier. That is the defect LADDER Q/V removed from D1. The D0 formula-group spreads (0.46–10 kcal/mol in large groups) and the 14 negative-d rows suggest D0 has the same defect. The other 7 targets (elst, pauli, oi, disp, cpcm, cds, c_ghost) use only TS-geometry calculations and are fully consistent.

There is no D0 equivalent of LADDER Phase V (DFT conformer search). The Q step (regrouping existing e_frag*_rel_eh by molecule key) needs no QM. Matching cr2 exactly would also need V for D0, which is new ORCA work. On D1, V found a lower conformer for only 30 of 177 targeted molecules and 0 of 20 controls (835 allocated core-h).

The D0 molecule key needs a constrained/alt state. D1 Q-2 read 'constrained' from D1 ref_result.json. D0 records only have alt_used and the _alt filename, and no ref_result.json exists. The constrained status for D0 would have to be taken from the Coley profiles or decided as a rule.

The TS-engine offset between D0 (G16) and D1 (ORCA RIJCOSX) is small for barrier, d1, d2, disp, cpcm and cds (mean |Δ| <= 0.08). It is larger for pauli and oi (RMS 1.6 / 0.8, n = 24, driven by one reaction). It largely cancels inside D0–D0 pairs but not in D0–D1 cross pairs. Reference geometries also differ by engine, so the same molecule (e.g. ethylene, or the 5 overlapping reactions) has different E_ref in D0 and D1.

c_ghost column choice: S_targets dft_c_ghost_kcal is a derived value that differs from bsse_shift_kcal by up to about 1e-9 (identity residual). D1 uses bsse_shift_kcal directly. A gate like L-11 (1e-12) would flag the difference if dft_c_ghost_kcal is used.

D0 has no HF/6-31G* values. D1-HF and the GEO2 H step cover D1 only, so the SH arm baseline (β·ΔH, with d1/d2/barrier using the refs='min' rule) does not exist for D0 without new HF EDA runs. This concerns inputs rather than labels, but it blocks SH on D0.

The pair models (AW, GNN, TF, XGB) learn dd = y_a − y_b. F_pairs and S_folds hold only D1 within-family pairs (ref_kind, Xb, pos, sigma, fold_T1), and D0 has no designed families. D0 labels become dd targets only after D0 pairs are defined. Both reactions in a pair need the same reference rule, which again means correcting D0 d1/d2/barrier.
26 D0 rows fail hygiene, and 260 charged-dipolarophile rows are outside the D1 range (D1 is all neutral). The label definition is the same for these rows; whether to keep them is a training choice.

If GEO1b-predicted D0 structures are used for the geo rung, GEO1b was trained on the D0 label TSs (D0 is never a test fold). The D0 inputs would then come from an in-sample structure model. This is not a label issue, but it affects how D0 labels can be scored.
options: A (recommended): apply the LADDER Q rule to D0 with no QM, on an sbatch CPU job. Molecule keys come from full_dataset.csv rxn_smiles (RDKit canonical isomeric, enantiomers merged, dipole key extended by alt/constrained state). Use E_min of e_frag1_rel_eh / e_frag2_rel_eh, replace when > 0.05 kcal/mol, and re-assemble d1/d2/barrier with the refs_q.py functions and gates Q-a…Q-e. Output labels_d0_cr.json / F_pairs-style D0 labels. Variant A2: build the keys over D0 ∪ D1 together, so shared molecules use one minimum. Same SP level, so the energies are comparable; record the G16-vs-ORCA reference geometry.
B: A plus a D0 Phase V (refs_v.py conformer search on D0 molecules with dev > 0.5, plus a control group), giving a true D0 cr2. New ORCA cost; on D1 V changed only 123 fragments.

C: use D0 labels as they are (labels_all.json, Coley-rule references). The 7 reference-independent targets are fully consistent. d1/d2/barrier follow a different rule from the D1 cr2 y, and this has to be stated as a deviation.
D: train elst, pauli, oi, disp, cpcm, cds and c_ghost on D0 + D1, and train d1, d2 and barrier on D1 only, or on D0 only after A.

Whichever option is chosen: read targets from labels_all.json with D1_TCOL key names (c_ghost = bsse_shift_kcal), not from S_targets dft_c_ghost_kcal. Use status == 'ok' (5,260), drop the 5 D1-overlap reactions, apply the same hygiene rule as D1 (26 rows), and decide whether to keep the 260 charged rows. Compare the 8 D1 / 5 D0 overlap reactions as a free empirical check of the D0-vs-D1 label offset per target.
investigations.recommendation: D0 has all 10 targets in labels_all.json: 5,260 usable rows, 5,255 after removing the 5 reactions that overlap D1, and 5,234 pass the d1/d2 hygiene rule. The single-point method, solvation, units, parser and assembly method ① are identical to D1. Seven targets (elst, pauli, oi, disp, cpcm, cds, c_ghost = bsse_shift_kcal) can be used directly. d1, d2 and barrier cannot: the D1 answers (F_pairs_cr2.csv / labels_d1_cr2.json) use the lowest reference per molecule (Q + V), while D0 uses Coley's per-reaction references. Before training, re-assemble D0 d1, d2 and barrier with the LADDER Q rule (option A, preferably over D0 ∪ D1 keys). This needs no QM and its gates are already written (refs_q.py). Record the missing D0 Phase V as a deviation, or run option B if exact cr2 parity is required. Read D0 targets with the D1_TCOL key names (bsse_shift_kcal, not the derived dft_c_ghost_kcal). Use the 8 D1 / 5 D0 overlap reactions as a free check of the remaining G16-vs-ORCA geometry offset, which is small except for pauli and oi. Two separate blockers sit outside the labels: D0 has no HF values for the SH arm, and D0 pairs must be defined for the pair models.

Model maths (analysis/d1_pair/fu2/models.py, d1_train.py): AW g = E(a) - E(b), with E = sum of atom contributions + phi(glob). GNN and TF g = 1/2[h(r_a,r_b) - h(r_b,r_a)]. XGB is trained on (z, y) and (-dx, -y) and predicts g = 1/2[h(dx,xbar) - h(-dx,xbar)], with z = [dx/s_delta, (xbar-mu)/s] from d1_train.Scale on the training pairs. SH arm: beta_t = sum(dH*dy)/sum(dH^2) on the fit's own pairs. All four models are exactly antisymmetric for any (a, b), so the maths assumes nothing about how pairs are formed. FU2 training flips (a,b) at random in each epoch (epoch_batches).

Current uses of D0 are all absolute. d1_f0.py: f0 = Ridge/KRR/SVR/XGB/NN2/NN4 trained on the 4,963 D0 rows (rev 6 appendix A, X182_all.parquet, S_targets dft_* columns) and frozen; it feeds arm A (delta f0) and arm B (g learns dd - delta f0). d1_train.py arm P: one KRR on D0 4,963 + training-side D1 reactions, predicting f(a) - f(b), with D0 in every inner-training fold and never in validation.

GEO1b (analysis/geo1b/train.py split, train_m1.py): D0 records carry core 'D0', fold -1, and sit in the training set of every model (all except the 5 overlaps). Final predictions are written only for the D1 test fold, so no D0 geo structures exist, and every GEO1b model has seen every D0 reaction. The GEO2.md section 3 (Phase Y) rule says training inputs must come from a refiner that did not see that reaction (Y costs about 15 GPU-h, GEO1B.md line 1756).
D0 has no HF/6-31G* H values (D1-HF and D1-G2 H were D1 only), no FU2 tokens, and no X182 features on G2 or geo structures (X182_all.parquet was computed on the rev 6 TS).
problems: The LADDER loaders reject an extended pair table by design. train_atoms.py / train_xgb.py require the label file to equal F_pairs.csv except dd_d1/dd_d2/dd_barrier (L-11). The split files T1__f<k>.json and splits/pairs.parquet are sha256-checked against FU2 S_splits.json, and Data / XData load only those lists. Adding D0 pairs needs a new label file, new split files and a narrower invariant (D1 rows byte-identical, extra rows with ref_kind 'd0').

Inner folds: GroupKFold(4) by core runs on the outer-training list. A D0 core would fall entirely into one inner_val fold and would also reshuffle the D1 inner folds. That breaks XG-4 (fold 0 must equal the split file), L-9 (atom and XGB validation pairs must match) and the D1-only meaning of validation MAE used for REP. D0 must be left out of the GroupKFold call and added to every inner_train, as arm P does.

Scale mismatch: D0 pair |dd| is 2.5-6 times D1's, so s_y grows. XGB uses reg:squarederror (train_ml_single GRIDS['XGB']), so D0 pairs would dominate its loss. The SH beta (least squares through the origin) would be set mostly by D0's large dH. The FU2 tuning normaliser SD(original y) also changes per target. FU2's L1 loss is less affected.

Structure leak: D0 geo coordinates from the GEO1b final models would be in-sample, because every model trained on all of D0. This breaks the Phase Y principle. D0 needs out-of-sample refiner predictions, or G2c structures.

Missing D0 inputs on the geo rung: phase G (xTB Freq for B6), phase F (X182, atoms, tokens) and phase H (HF EDA, 5 single points for each of roughly 4.5-5.2k reactions; with median 44 vs 35 atoms, each costs about 2x a D1 reaction). Without H, the usable filter would silently drop every D0 pair from the SH arm.

Label references differ. D1 y uses cr2 references (the lowest conformer per molecule key, after the V search). D0 labels_all uses the Coley references with no Q/V check. In pairs where the varied reactant differs, dd_d1/dd_d2/dd_barrier carry reference noise; in sibling pairs it cancels exactly. The D1 row rules (ex > 20, flag_async with 231 D0 rows, hygiene) and removal of the 5 overlaps have not yet been applied to D0.

D0 has no X / family / regio labels (regio, R1 and R2 are blank), so D1's 'same TS class, one substituent changed' family cannot be rebuilt from metadata. Pairs across different dipolarophiles are large, very unlike D1's test pairs.

Absolute D0 training cannot be done with the models as they are. GNN and TF have no single-reaction output; AW would need a new loss and is already equivalent to pair training up to one constant per connected component; XGB absolute is f0, which failed in rev 9. D0-D1 cross pairs would make pair lists fold-dependent (leak risk) and mix cr2 with Coley references, while covering only about 400 D0 rows.

Compute and checks: training pairs per fold grow 33-70% (from about 6.3-6.6k T_main) and the largest reaction grows from 63 to 94 atoms (GNN/TF are O(N^2)). That puts the GEO2 M3 cap of 80 GPU-h at risk. Gate M-1' samples only test pairs, so D0 pairs, which are never tested, would never be checked.
options: A. D0 sibling pairs only. Key = (dipole_smiles, dipolarophile_smiles); anchor = the first reaction by hygiene-pass, then lowest rxn_id; a = every other row. Gives 2,096 pairs from 3,383 rows. Reference energies cancel exactly, the pairs isolate TS-geometry differences (what geo changes), |dd| is the smallest of the D0 options, and the sibling-pair precedent exists in REV9 0-1. About 25% of D0 rows stay unused.

B. Hierarchical D0 anchor forest, following d1_anchor_pairs.py. Edges are added by priority: siblings, then same dipole (like D1's R2 series), then same dipolarophile (like R1). Each group keeps a deterministic anchor (hygiene-pass, then fewest heavy atoms on the varied reactant, then lowest rxn_id). Each D0 reaction is 'a' exactly once, giving rows-with-partner minus components pairs: between 3,820 and about 4,400 on the 4,491 G2-done rows, covering at least 97% of them. A column edge_kind records sibling / dipole / dipolarophile.
C. Anchor pairs on a single key: same dipolarophile (3,820 pairs, 4,342 rows, mean |dd_barrier| 9.1) or same dipole (2,848 pairs, 3,948 rows, 5.0).

D. Absolute per-reaction D0. Works only for XGB (it is the d1_f0 setup, which failed in rev 9). AW would need an extra E(a) ~ y_a loss and GNN/TF a new single-reaction head, so this is not the four LADDER models as they are.

That weakens the T1 claim ('unseen (dipole, skeleton) combination') for the energy result. D1PAIR accepted this only for f0 and arm P, never for the LADDER atom models.

D-1 matching includes the product, so it misses regio and stereo siblings. A D0 reaction with the same reactants as a D1 test reaction but the other regiochemistry is not flagged and would stay in training if D0 is train-only. Core-based fold assignment covers this automatically; train-only does not.

D0 inside D1 fold -1 cores: D1 pairs of those 6 cores are training pairs in every energy fold. So a D0 test pair from such a core would face its own core in training. Those D0 reactions must be energy train-only, and their refined structures must still come from a model that held them out (the Y model, if it is extended to them).

Mapping D0 to D1 cores needs new deterministic RDKit code (dipole type x dipolarophile scaffold and substitution pattern at the D1 granularity A/Ap/AppE/AppZ/B/Bp/C/Cp/D/Dp) run as a CPU sbatch job. mmp_utils gives only dclass (dipole ring atoms). An unmapped D0 reaction that really belongs to a D1 test core would leak, so the rule must lean toward merging when unsure.

D0 pairs can cross cores: an MMP dph_change such as H to Me on a reacting carbon changes A to Ap. Such pairs (90 of 4,536 in rev4 are dph_change) must be dropped when their two reactions land in different folds. Pair yield on the geo rung is not known yet. It needs both reactions with G2c, a refined TS, features and HF; a rough estimate from 0.853^2 is about 70 % of 4,536.

Inner validation and REP selection: LADDER val_kcal_mae (REP / REP8 per target) is computed on D1 inner_val pairs. If D0 pairs enter inner_train without core-consistent inner grouping, inner_val becomes optimistic. If D0 pairs enter inner_val, the selection rule changes meaning.

D0 test metrics are not comparable to D1 P_main: D0 pairs are MMP pairs (not Hammett series), the label TSs come from a different engine (G16 vs ORCA), and the d1/d2/barrier reference conventions differ from F_pairs_cr2 (refs='min'). D0 results should be reported separately and should not feed the D1 primary metric.
options: Structure option S-A (fold-aligned D0 inside GEO1b; no extra GPU). Give every D0 reaction a fold label: the T1 fold of its D1 core when it maps to one (including -1), otherwise 0-4 by the d1_split rule (sorted D0-only cores, rng(20261019) permutation, fewest pairs or reactions so far). Change GEO1b split(k): tune train excludes D0 of folds k and (k+1)%5; final trains on D1 + D0 of folds other than k and predicts D1 + D0 of fold k (3-seed mean, as for D1). Extend Y: test = D1 + D0 of fold -1; train = D1 + D0 of fold >= 0. U-9b gains the check 'no D0 of fold k in fold-k training'. The task count stays at 41 (tune 20, select 5, final 15, eval 1) plus Y. Training sets shrink by about 1/5 of D0 (final) and 2/5 (tune), so R costs slightly less than the about 240 GPU-h estimate. Every D0 reaction gets exactly one out-of-sample refined TS, and the stage-1 D0 core leak against D1 tests also goes away.

Structure option S-B (keep GEO1b exactly as specified, add separate D0 cross-fold refiners). For each D0 fold k, train a refiner on D1 folds other than k + D0 folds other than k with Y_plan epochs, 3 seeds: 15 runs x about 4.6 (GEO1b estimate) to 6.9 (GEO1 measured) GPU-h = about 70-105 GPU-h, plus 3 more Y-style runs if D0 maps to fold -1 cores. With 1 seed: 5 runs, about 25-35 GPU-h, but D0 would then be 1-seed while D1 is a 3-seed mean, which is inconsistent. This duplicates GEO1b's finals with nearly the same training sets, and D1 tests keep the stage-1 D0 core leak.

Structure option S-C (no refiner for D0: use G2c TSs for D0 in the geo rung). Costs 0 GPU, but D0 would be on unrefined inputs while D1 is on refined inputs. This mixes input distributions in one energy model. Not recommended.
Structure option S-D (in-sample GEO1b predictions for D0). Costs 0 GPU but repeats the mismatch GEO2.md section 3 rejected for D1 fold -1. Not recommended.

Energy fold option E-1 (D0 train-only: every D0 pair is fold -1 in all 5 units, D1 T1 folds unchanged). This is the simplest and matches the D1PAIR f0 / arm P precedent; inner val and REP stay D1-only. Drawbacks: D0 of D1 test cores sits in training (T1 core claim weakened), the regio siblings issue remains, and there is no D0 result. If chosen, D0 structures still need S-A or S-B, because train-only pairs must not use in-sample structures.

Energy fold option E-2 (recommended, core-aligned D0 folds, D0 also tested). Use the same D0 fold label as S-A. Fold-k test = D1 fold-k P_sens and A_main (unchanged) + D0 MMP pairs with both reactions in fold k. Train = D1 T_main + D0 pairs of the other folds. D0 of D1 fold -1 cores = train-only. Cross-fold D0 pairs are dropped. Inner GroupKFold(4) by core over D1 cores and D0 cores together (D0 of mapped cores follows its D1 core), with REP / val_kcal_mae selection computed on D1 inner_val pairs only, so LADDER 13-1 keeps its meaning. Generate new T1+D0 split files with their own sha record and gate, and keep the LADDER leak checks (test reaction never in training pairs). Report D0 MAE separately from D1 P_main.

Energy fold option E-3 (D0 folds by D0-only grouping, such as dclass or connected MMP components, ignoring the D1 cores). No classifier is needed, but D0 and D1 of the same core land in different folds, which brings back core leakage in both directions. Not recommended.

D-1 handling: (a) keep it (exclude the 5 D0 reactions everywhere: GEO1b, Y, energy pairs). This is consistent with 'all data used in GEO1' (D1 9,266 + D0 5,255) and required under E-1, because 3 of the copies are base reactions of 174 fold-2 test pairs. (b) Drop the exclusion under E-2 and S-A, since the copies would map into the same fold-1/2 cores as their D1 twins and so cannot leak across folds. That would change the GEO1b D-report gate (d0_overlap 5) and double-weight 5 reactions. (c) Additionally run a reactant-only check (sorted reactants, no product, no stereo) as a report-only sensitivity, to count the regio and stereo siblings that D-1 misses.

design.recommended_design:
D1 (9,266 reactions) and D0 (5,255 = the 5,260 status-ok rows of labels_all.json minus the 5 reactions GEO1 rule D-1 excludes) both run the whole pipeline: G2c, then the GEO1b structure refiner, then geo inputs, then energy. The energy step is the four LADDER pair-difference models (AW, GNN, TF, XGB), each with arms S and SH, trained once on rung geo. The g2 and dft rungs are not retrained, and the GEO2.md 10 geo-vs-g2 verdict is dropped. This follows the user request and reuses existing code; the changes are data plumbing and one GEO1b split rule.

KEY IDEA: before GEO1b R starts (it has not; it waits on g2c_build 1055745), give every D0 reaction one fold 0-4 and use that same fold in both stages.
(1) Structures. GEO1b final_f{k} trains without D0 fold k and predicts D1 fold k plus D0 fold k. Every D0 geo TS then comes from a model that never saw it, at zero extra GPU. Today every GEO1b model trains on all D0, so any D0 geo TS would be in-sample, which GEO2.md 3 forbids.
(2) Energy. D0 pairs train in the 4 units whose test fold differs from their own and are tested in the 5th. This gives a D0 result from the same 40 units, next to the unchanged D1 T1 result.

LABELS
- D0 targets come from labels_all.json with the D1_TCOL key names (c_ghost = bsse_shift_kcal, not the derived S_targets dft_c_ghost_kcal).
- d1, d2 and barrier are re-assembled with the LADDER Q rule: refs_q.py molecule_keys / audit / choose_override / assemble, no QM. Keys are built within D0. A reference read from an *_alt.xyz file gets its own '|alt' key. The Q-2 bond-graph check applies. Replace when the gap is > 0.05 kcal/mol.
- This puts D0 on the same lowest-reference rule as the D1 cr2 labels. There is no D0 Phase V (DFT conformer search); this is recorded as a deviation.
- The other 7 targets are reference-free and used as they are. The D1 labels (y) stay F_pairs_cr2.csv, byte-identical.

D0 PAIRS (new d0_pairs.py, modelled on d1_anchor_pairs.py)
- Component = one dipole molecule (stereo-free canonical SMILES from d0_manifest dipole_smiles).
- Inside a component, a deterministic anchor tree:
  - regio/stereo siblings (same dipolarophile) pair with their sibling-set anchor;
  - sibling-set anchors pair with the component anchor (same dipole, different dipolarophile);
  - a D0 reaction whose dipole occurs nowhere else attaches as a leaf to a same-dipolarophile reaction and joins that component.
- Edges link only reactions with equal charge1 and charge2.
- Anchor priority: has a G2c TS, then passes hygiene, then lowest rxn_id.
- Each component gives n-1 pairs, and every pair stays inside one fold. Expect about 3,000-3,500 pairs.
- The D1 row rules apply to D0 pairs: flag_async, ex1/ex2 > 20 on the Coley references, and R6 hygiene on the Q labels. The 260 charged rows are kept.
- Components get folds by the d1_split greedy balance (rng 20261019).
- 'Twins' are D0 reactions with the same stereo-free reactant set as a D1 reaction (other than the 5 D-1 overlaps). A twin takes its D1 twin's fold (0-4), so it is never trained on when the twin is tested.
- D0 has no fold -1.

GEO1b PATCH
- data.py reads d0_folds.csv.
- train.py split(k): D0 with fold != k goes into both tune and final training; final_f{k} predicts D1 fold k plus D0 fold k.
- select still uses the D1 inner-validation pairs (all para pairs).
- Y (train_m1) is unchanged: it predicts D1 fold -1 only.
- Still 41 tasks plus 3 Y runs.

GEO2b INPUTS
- One combined root for D1 and D0: geo_final, then G (xTB Freq), F (X182 + FU2 tokens) and H (HF/6-31G* EDA).
- D0 HF templates are built with prep.hf_text from the SMD inputs: eda_smd_relabel/inputs/rxn_NNNN/eda.inp and label_true/work/inputs/rxn_NNNN/frag*.inp.
- P (input table): refs='min' over the union of the D1 Q keys and the new D0 Q keys.

TRAINING
- New label file F_pairs_d0d1.csv = F_pairs_cr2.csv rows unchanged, plus D0 rows with ref_kind 'd0' and ids D#####.
- New split files T1D0__f<k>.json:
  - the D1 lists equal the FU2 T1__f<k> lists exactly;
  - D0 pairs of the other folds are added to train and to every inner_train;
  - D0 pairs of fold k are added to test;
  - inner_val stays D1 only, so REP and REP8 keep their LADDER 13-1 meaning.
- Model code, grids, loss, beta rule, seeds, epochs and patience are unchanged. L-11 becomes 'D1 rows identical to F_pairs_cr2.csv; extra rows ref_kind d0'.
- 2 arms x 4 models x 5 folds = 40 units.

RESULTS (reported separately, never pooled)
- D1: P_geo para P_main pairs plus all positions; each of the 4 models x 2 arms, REP, REP8 and ENS4; core bootstrap 95% CI; the LADDER stage-2 absolute goal (oi and cpcm para MAE <= 0.13 kcal/mol, plus the bend criterion).
- D0: the fold-held-out D0 test pairs; the same model and selection tables; component bootstrap CI; broken down by edge kind.

RISKS ACCEPTED, RECORDED AS LIMITATIONS
- Cross-fold dependence of the structure models (GEO2.md 10-3) now covers D0 as well.
- D0 reactions of the same dipole/dipolarophile type as D1 test cores sit in training. This is cross-dataset transfer, not label leakage, but it weakens the T1 'unseen core' claim.

When it finishes, run one sbatch job (cpu1/cpu2, 1 CPU, 48:00:00) for /usr/lpp/mmfs/bin/mmlsquota. STOP if less than 40 GB is free: the geo_final folders for about 14k reactions, the HF run folders and the tokens need roughly 20-30 GB.

1. D0 labels (Q rule). Write analysis/geo1b/d0_labels.py on branch geo1b; it imports analysis/d1_ladder/refs_q.py read only, in LADENV=reactot.
- Input: labels_all.json status-ok rows (5,260).

- data.py make_rec: a D0 record gets core 'D0/<component>' and the fold from d0_folds.csv.
- train.py split(k): D0 joins tune and final training only if fold != k.
- train.py final: predict eval_items for D1 fold k + D0 fold k; write final_f{k}_s{seed}.pkl as before.
- tests.py U-9b, extended:
  - no D0 of fold k (or twin of fold k) in fold-k tune or final training;
  - every non-overlap D0 reaction with a G2c TS is predicted exactly once, by its own fold model;
  - the 5 overlaps are in no training set.
- evaluate.py: D1 metrics unchanged; add a descriptive E_rxn_d0.csv (forming-bond errors) so build_geo can cross-check D0.
- train_m1.py: unchanged.

4. GEO1b run, as in GEO1B.md 3 with the A-G2c reading.
- D: gb_data. D0 G2 count = the G2c count.
- U: tests.py synth and tests.py data.
- R: r_launch.py. Tasks: 20 tune, 5 select, 15 final, 1 eval. Use up to 10 GPU slots, since G2c is done by then.
- E1 (evaluate.py) and E2 (rmsd_b.py, sanity_fail_share <= 0.02).
- Y: train_m1.py plan, then final 0, 1 and 2 with GEO_MAX_EP=300 and GEO_PATIENCE=100000. Y can run alongside the finals.
- Write SUMMARY_GEO1B.md (descriptive, D1 tables plus a D0 descriptive table), commit and push.

8. P: build $GEO2B/inputs/geo.parquet over D1 + D0. Keys are the union of $LAD/Q_keys.parquet and Q_keys_d0.parquet; P6b checks formula and WL hash against each dataset's label references. Write P_geo_report.json: usable reactions and pairs per dataset and fold, and the D0 pairs lost because an endpoint is unusable.

9. Label and split files, plus the trainer changes.
- $GEO2B/F_pairs_d0d1.csv: F_pairs_cr2.csv rows byte-identical, then D0 rows in the same columns. D1-only columns are empty; fam/core = 'D0/<component>'.
- $GEO2B/splits/T1D0__f<k>.json and analysis/geo2/results/S_splits_d0d1.json with sha256.
- train_atoms.py and train_xgb.py:
  - add rung geo (GEO2.md 8-1) and split 'T1D0' (load_folds from S_splits_d0d1.json);
  - L-11': D1 rows equal F_pairs_cr2.csv; D0 rows equal D0_pairs.csv, with provenance from the Q_d0_report sha;
  - the D1 subsets of the new split lists must equal the FU2 T1 lists exactly.
- Diagnostic only, no training: s_y and SH beta per fold, for D1 pairs alone and for D1 + D0.

11. Write PREREG_GEO2B.md and prereg json; commit and push before any training.
- Content: rung geo definition, D0 fold/pair rules, sha256 of labels / splits / inputs / d0_folds, metrics and selection rules (REP, REP8, ENS4 by D1 inner-val MAE), the LADDER goal as the only absolute target, the limitations, and GEO1b's descriptive numbers already seen.

Then train_atoms.py collect --stage 3 --with-xgb gives L_predictions_geo.parquet and L_report_geo.json / L_xgb_report_geo.json; existing LADDER files are sha256-checked as unchanged.

decisions_needing_user: Only one item needs a decision, and it has a default. GEO1B.md (user-approved) says D0 is never a test fold, so every GEO1b model trains on all of D0. With that rule, every D0 geo structure would be in-sample. The design changes it: each GEO1b final_f{k} model leaves out D0 fold k (it trains on 4/5 of D0) and predicts that fold. This is the only way to get out-of-sample D0 structures with no extra GPU. Default: apply it now, before GEO1b R starts. The alternative keeps GEO1b exactly as written and adds 15 separate D0 hold-out refiners: about 70-105 GPU-h and about 1 more day. Every other branch takes the recommended option and is recorded in DECISIONS: Q rule on D0 with no D0 Phase V, D0 also scored by fold, charged rows kept, no D0 sample weights, H cap raised to 4,000 core-h and M3 cap to 160 GPU-h.
risks: No comparison model is trained, as the user asked, so nobody can measure whether adding D0 helps or hurts D1 accuracy. D0 pair differences are 2.5-6x larger than D1's (mean |dd_barrier| 4-5 vs 1.57 kcal/mol). They may dominate the XGB squared loss, the SH beta (least squares through the origin) and s_y. Only the s_y / beta diagnostic (D1-only vs D1+D0) is reported. The existing LADDER g2/dft numbers come from different structures and are not a controlled comparison.

Core-level overlap. D0 reactions of the same dipole x dipolarophile type as a D1 test core (for example D0 nitrone + alkene while D1 nitrone/A is tested) sit in training. This is cross-dataset transfer, not label leakage, but the D1 T1 'unseen core' claim weakens and must be stated. The 5 exact copies stay excluded, and reactant-level twins follow their D1 twin's fold.
Cross-fold dependence of the structure stage (GEO2.md 10-3) now also covers D0. Training-pair structures come from refiners that saw the label TSs of the test fold, though never its energy labels.

D0 label quality. Q is applied without a D0 Phase V. The '|alt' key rule is new; D1 used a ref_port constrained flag that D0 lacks. D0 label TSs are Gaussian 16 and D1's are ORCA RIJCOSX; A5-eng shows small offsets except pauli and oi (RMS 1.6 / 0.8 kcal/mol, n = 24). D0 and D1 results must be reported separately, never pooled.

D0 inputs are new and only partly checked. No D0 X182 reference exists (the G1 folders were deleted). The D0 HF templates are validated only by the 3-reaction S-1 check plus the X checks. D0 adds 260 charged reactions and 285 reactions larger than any D1 reaction, so Freq, Q-a and HF SCF failure rates may rise.
Compute. GNN/TF cost grows about 2x per batch at n_max 94, and M3 may exceed the 160 GPU-h projection. The whole chain is blocked behind the still-running G2c D0 r1/r2 roots and g2c_build.

Code-change surface. The LADDER loaders are sha-locked (S_splits, L-11, XG-4, L-9). The new T1D0 split and L-11' must leave the D1 lists byte-identical. Regression tests 1-3 and the before/after sha256 of existing LADDER result files guard this.

D0 coverage depends on G2c and geo usability, since a pair is lost when either endpoint is unusable. The expected D0 pair count (about 3,000-3,500) is fixed only when d0_pairs.py runs. The pair structure is a star around each anchor, so a few anchors that fail later remove whole groups of pairs; the anchor rule prefers reactions that have a G2c TS to limit this.
